elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph says only "Contractor shall indemnify Company against any third-party claim..."; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to Company's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Indemnity runs to "Company" only; affiliates are not named as beneficiaries.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — Works is the Agreement's deliverables concept (see 5(c)).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The inserted indemnity is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no breach-of-law trigger.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised access/disclosure of Company data trigger appears in the inserted paragraph or elsewhere in Section 7.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in the inserted language.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no notice mechanic.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of defence control; the only "at its option" language concerns the procure/modify/replace remedies.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the Agreement contains no Company-side indemnity at all (a document search for "indemn" returns only the Section 7 heading and the new insertion), so there is no broader Customer indemnity to narrow; the position is at least as favourable as the limit required.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall indemnify Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent the claim arises from Company's modification of the Services or Works" — permissive exclusion, within the fallback's allowance.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "Company's combination of the Services or Works with items not supplied by Contractor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall, at its option, procure for Company the right to continue using, modify, or replace the affected item" — mandatory obligation with Contractor's choice among the three customary remedies.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, Contractor shall refund the fees paid for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Contractor's aggregate liability under this Paragraph 7(d) shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid to Contractor under this Agreement", and 7(a) was conformed ("EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 7(d) OR PARAGRAPH 9") so the fees-paid cap does not swallow the super-cap.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: Section 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but 7(a)-(c) contain only liability caps, a damages allocation and an attorneys'-fee waiver, and the only IP hook is the bare non-infringement warranty in 5(c). No Contractor IP indemnity existed, which is walk-away territory, so a redline is warranted.
All seven fallback elements are met in operative language: IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions, the procure/modify/replace remedy ladder, a refund fallback, and a 3x annual fees super-cap.

Preferred level is not reached: the insertion has no express duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, and no notice/control/cooperation procedure. The Customer-indemnity element passes only because no Company-side indemnity exists to narrow.

Minimality holds: the only collateral edit is the narrow conforming carve-out in 7(a) ("PARAGRAPH 7(d) OR"), which is necessary for the super-cap element to have effect; the drafter added no survival tail, no attorneys'-fee or damages language, no claims procedure and no Company-side indemnity, and retained 7(a)'s Company-favourable cap on Company's own liability, 7(c) and the 5(c) warranty unchanged.
Intent is preserved: the third-party indemnity does not conflict with 7(c)'s waiver of attorneys' fees in suits between the parties, and the pre-existing Paragraph 9 carve-out in 7(a) survives.

Drafting fix (not an element failure): the inserted paragraph is rendered without a "(d)" designator while both the amended 7(a) and the paragraph itself refer to "Paragraph 7(d)". Label the insertion "(d)" expressly so the cross-reference is not dangling.
Optional escalation if the counterparty engages: add "defend" and "and its affiliates" plus a short notice/control/cooperation mechanic to move from fallback toward the preferred position.
